'''Endre Boros''' (born 21 September 1953) is a Hungarian-American mathematician, a distinguished professor at [[Rutgers University]] in New Brunswick, New Jersey, and the director of the Center for Operations Research (RUTCOR).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rutcor.rutgers.edu/EBoros.htm |title=Endre Boros |publisher=Rutcor.rutgers.edu |date= |access-date=2012-11-28}}</ref>   He is the author of 15 book chapters and edited volumes, and 165 research papers. He is associate editor of the Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, and Editor-in-Chief of both the Annals of Operations Research and Discrete Applied Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/discrete-applied-mathematics/editorial-board/endre-boros/ |title=Endre Boros, Editor-in-Chief - Discrete Applied Mathematics |publisher=Journals.elsevier.com |date= |access-date=2012-11-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/business+%26+management/operations+research/journal/10479 |title=Annals of Operations Research – incl. option to publish open access |publisher=Springer.com |date= |access-date=2012-11-28}}</ref>

==Results==
{{harvtxt|Boros|Szőnyi|1986}} settled a conjecture by [[Beniamino Segre]] about the cyclic structure of [[finite projective plane]]s, and {{harvtxt|Boros|1988}} provided the best known bound for a question posed by [[Paul Erdős]] about blocking sets of Galois planes. {{harvtxt|Boros|Gurvich|1996}} proved that [[perfect graph]]s are kernel solvable which answered a longstanding open question by C. Berge and P. Duchet (and which is independent of the [[perfect graph theorem]]). He settled the complexity of generating all maximal frequent and minimal infrequent sets of large data sets answering questions by R.H. Sloan, K. Takata and G. Turán in {{harvtxt|Boros|Gurvich|Khachiyan|Makino|2003}}, and in {{harvtxt|Khachiyan|Boros|Borys|Elbassioni|2008}} resolved the complexity of the longstanding open problem of generating all vertices of polyhedra.

{{harvtxt|Boros|Hammer|Sun|Tavares|2008}} uses a [[flow network|network flow]] based approach for quadratic binary optimization.
In the area of the theory of [[Horn function]]s, {{harvtxt|Boros|Crama|Hammer|1990}} proved that all "prime implicates" of a Horn CNF can be generated efficiently, extended Horn logic to q-Horn and showed that this extension forms in some sense the boundary between tractable and intractable logic.
